sanskrit: kayā̍ naś ci̱tra ā bhu̍vad ū̱tī sa̱dāvṛ̍dha̱ḥ sakhā̍ | kayā̱ śaci̍ṣṭhayā vṛ̱tā ||
english: By what aid shall the wondrous one, the ever-strengthening Friend, come to our help? With what most powerful deed, attended?

sanskrit: kas tvā̍ sa̱tyo madā̍nā̱m maṁhi̍ṣṭho matsa̱d andha̍saḥ | dṛ̱ḻhā ci̍d ā̱ruje̱ vasu̍ ||
english: Which true exhilaration, most bounteous, shall gladden you with the soma-draught? You who break open even firm strongholds to release their wealth.

sanskrit: a̱bhī ṣu ṇa̱ḥ sakhī̍nām avi̱tā ja̍ritṝ̱ṇām | śa̱tam bha̍vāsy ū̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Be a hundredfold protector to us, the friends of your praisers, with your aids.

sanskrit: a̱bhī na̱ ā va̍vṛtsva ca̱kraṁ na vṛ̱ttam arva̍taḥ | ni̱yudbhi̍ś carṣaṇī̱nām ||
english: Turn toward us, like a wheel rolled back from the steed, with your swift teams that serve among men.

sanskrit: pra̱vatā̱ hi kratū̍nā̱m ā hā̍ pa̱deva̱ gaccha̍si | abha̍kṣi̱ sūrye̱ sacā̍ ||
english: Along the downward slope of mighty deeds you come — as a footprint — and you have had your share together with the Sun.

sanskrit: saṁ yat ta̍ indra ma̱nyava̱ḥ saṁ ca̱krāṇi̍ dadhanvi̱re | adha̱ tve adha̱ sūrye̍ ||
english: When, O Indra, your wraths surge together and your chariot-wheels rush forward — then it is in you and in the Sun.

sanskrit: u̱ta smā̱ hi tvām ā̱hur in ma̱ghavā̍naṁ śacīpate | dātā̍ra̱m avi̍dīdhayum ||
english: For they speak of you as the bountiful lord of power, O Śacīpati, the giver who never lets the worshippers down.

sanskrit: u̱ta smā̍ sa̱dya it pari̍ śaśamā̱nāya̍ sunva̱te | pu̱rū ci̍n maṁhase̱ vasu̍ ||
english: And verily, forthwith, to him who has labored and pressed the soma, you grant manifold wealth.

sanskrit: na̱hi ṣmā̍ te śa̱taṁ ca̱na rādho̱ vara̍nta ā̱mura̍ḥ | na cyau̱tnāni̍ kariṣya̱taḥ ||
english: Not even a hundred rash foes can hold back your bounty or obstruct your mighty deeds.

sanskrit: a̱smām̐ a̍vantu te śa̱tam a̱smān sa̱hasra̍m ū̱taya̍ḥ | a̱smān viśvā̍ a̱bhiṣṭa̍yaḥ ||
english: May your hundredfold aids defend us, may your thousandfold aids uphold us, may all your favors come to us.

sanskrit: a̱smām̐ i̱hā vṛ̍ṇīṣva sa̱khyāya̍ sva̱staye̍ | ma̱ho rā̱ye di̱vitma̍te ||
english: Choose us here for friendship and well-being, for great wealth that shines with radiance.

sanskrit: a̱smām̐ a̍viḍḍhi vi̱śvahendra̍ rā̱yā parī̍ṇasā | a̱smān viśvā̍bhir ū̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Urge us forward, O Indra who are present everywhere, with abundant riches and with all your aids.

sanskrit: a̱smabhya̱ṁ tām̐ apā̍ vṛdhi vra̱jām̐ aste̍va̱ goma̍taḥ | navā̍bhir indro̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Open for us those cattle-pens as a bowman opens them, O Indra, with your fresh and ever-new aids.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̍ṁ dhṛṣṇu̱yā ratho̍ dyu̱mām̐ i̱ndrāna̍pacyutaḥ | ga̱vyur a̍śva̱yur ī̍yate ||
english: Our bold chariot, radiant and unshaken by Indra's side, goes forth seeking cattle and horses.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̍m utta̱maṁ kṛ̍dhi̱ śravo̍ de̱veṣu̍ sūrya | varṣi̍ṣṭha̱ṁ dyām i̍vo̱pari̍ ||
english: Make our glory the highest among the gods, O Sun, supremely lofty as the sky above.

sanskrit: ā tū na̍ indra vṛtrahann a̱smāka̍m a̱rdham ā ga̍hi | ma̱hān ma̱hībhi̍r ū̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Come to our side, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, come to us; great one, with great aids.

sanskrit: bhṛmi̍ś cid ghāsi̱ tūtu̍ji̱r ā ci̍tra ci̱triṇī̱ṣv ā | ci̱traṁ kṛ̍ṇoṣy ū̱taye̍ ||
english: Even the restless one you consume quickly, O wondrous one; among the marvelous you are marvelous, and you perform marvels for our help.

sanskrit: da̱bhrebhi̍ś ci̱c chaśī̍yāṁsa̱ṁ haṁsi̱ vrādha̍nta̱m oja̍sā | sakhi̍bhi̱r ye tve sacā̍ ||
english: With few allies you smite the great swaggering foe with your might — those who have the friends who go along with you.

sanskrit: va̱yam i̍ndra̱ tve sacā̍ va̱yaṁ tvā̱bhi no̍numaḥ | a̱smām̐-a̍smā̱m̐ id ud a̍va ||
english: We, O Indra, are at your side; we praise you continually. Uplift us, each and every one of us.

sanskrit: sa na̍ś ci̱trābhi̍r adrivo 'nava̱dyābhi̍r ū̱tibhi̍ḥ | anā̍dhṛṣṭābhi̱r ā ga̍hi ||
english: Come to us, O stone-wielder, with wondrous, blameless aids, with irresistible helps.

sanskrit: bhū̱yāmo̱ ṣu tvāva̍ta̱ḥ sakhā̍ya indra̱ goma̍taḥ | yujo̱ vājā̍ya̱ ghṛṣva̍ye ||
english: May we become your allies, O Indra, possessing cattle, yoked together for the battle-prize of glorious vigor.

sanskrit: tvaṁ hy eka̱ īśi̍ṣa̱ indra̱ vāja̍sya̱ goma̍taḥ | sa no̍ yandhi ma̱hīm iṣa̍m ||
english: For you alone, O Indra, are the lord of the battle-prize rich in cattle; bestow on us the great refreshment.

sanskrit: na tvā̍ varante a̱nyathā̱ yad ditsa̍si stu̱to ma̱gham | sto̱tṛbhya̍ indra girvaṇaḥ ||
english: They do not choose you otherwise than you grant the bounty when praised; to your praisers, O Indra, lover of songs.

sanskrit: a̱bhi tvā̱ gota̍mā gi̱rānū̍ṣata̱ pra dā̱vane̍ | indra̱ vājā̍ya̱ ghṛṣva̍ye ||
english: The Gotamas have praised you with their hymns for giving, O Indra, for the vigorous battle-prize.

sanskrit: pra te̍ vocāma vī̱ryā̱3̱̍ yā ma̍ndasā̱na āru̍jaḥ | puro̱ dāsī̍r a̱bhītya̍ ||
english: Let us proclaim your heroic deeds — how you, exhilarated, broke through the Dāsa strongholds, overcoming them.

sanskrit: tā te̍ gṛṇanti ve̱dhaso̱ yāni̍ ca̱kartha̱ pauṁsyā̍ | su̱teṣv i̍ndra girvaṇaḥ ||
english: The wise ones sing those manly deeds of yours at the soma-pressings, O Indra, lover of hymns.

sanskrit: avī̍vṛdhanta̱ gota̍mā̱ indra̱ tve stoma̍vāhasaḥ | aiṣu̍ dhā vī̱rava̱d yaśa̍ḥ ||
english: The Gotamas have grown strong through you, O Indra, bringing their hymns of praise; place hero-worthy glory in them.

sanskrit: yac ci̱d dhi śaśva̍tā̱m asīndra̱ sādhā̍raṇa̱s tvam | taṁ tvā̍ va̱yaṁ ha̍vāmahe ||
english: Though you are the common resort of all people always, O Indra, yet we call upon you specially.

sanskrit: a̱rvā̱cī̱no va̍so bhavā̱sme su ma̱tsvāndha̍saḥ | somā̍nām indra somapāḥ ||
english: Turn hither to us, O Vasu; be pleased with the soma-draughts, O drinker of Soma, O Indra.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̍ṁ tvā matī̱nām ā stoma̍ indra yacchatu | a̱rvāg ā va̍rtayā̱ harī̍ ||
english: May our hymn of praise draw you to us, O Indra; turn your two bay steeds hitherward.

sanskrit: pu̱ro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ ca no̱ ghaso̍ jo̱ṣayā̍se̱ gira̍ś ca naḥ | va̱dhū̱yur i̍va̱ yoṣa̍ṇām ||
english: You enjoy our oblation-cake and delight in our hymns, like a bridegroom eager for his bride.

sanskrit: sa̱hasra̱ṁ vyatī̍nāṁ yu̱ktānā̱m indra̍m īmahe | śa̱taṁ soma̍sya khā̱rya̍ḥ ||
english: We pray to Indra for a thousand teams of yoked horses and a hundred jars of soma.

sanskrit: sa̱hasrā̍ te śa̱tā va̱yaṁ gavā̱m ā cyā̍vayāmasi | a̱sma̱trā rādha̍ etu te ||
english: We shake loose from you thousands and hundreds of cattle; may your bounty come here to us.

sanskrit: daśa̍ te ka̱laśā̍nā̱ṁ hira̍ṇyānām adhīmahi | bhū̱ri̱dā a̍si vṛtrahan ||
english: We claim ten golden jars from you — you are a great giver, O slayer of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: bhūri̍dā̱ bhūri̍ dehi no̱ mā da̱bhram bhūry ā bha̍ra | bhūri̱ ghed i̍ndra ditsasi ||
english: O great giver, give us greatly; bring not a little but much; for you indeed are willing to give much, O Indra.

sanskrit: bhū̱ri̱dā hy asi̍ śru̱taḥ pu̍ru̱trā śū̍ra vṛtrahan | ā no̍ bhajasva̱ rādha̍si ||
english: For you are known as the great giver in many places, O hero, O slayer of Vṛtra; grant us a share in your bounty.

sanskrit: pra te̍ ba̱bhrū vi̍cakṣaṇa̱ śaṁsā̍mi goṣaṇo napāt | mābhyā̱ṁ gā anu̍ śiśrathaḥ ||
english: O clear-sighted grandson of the cattle-winner, I praise your two brown steeds; do not let the cattle go astray because of them.

sanskrit: ka̱nī̱na̱keva̍ vidra̱dhe nave̍ drupa̱de a̍rbha̱ke | ba̱bhrū yāme̍ṣu śobhete ||
english: Like young maidens adorned for the occasion on a newly planted footboard, the two bays look beautiful in their courses.

sanskrit: ara̍m ma u̱srayā̍mṇe 'ra̱m anu̍srayāmṇe | ba̱bhrū yāme̍ṣv a̱sridhā̍ ||
english: They are fit for the morning run, fit for the later run; the two bays never falter in their courses.

sanskrit: pra ṛ̱bhubhyo̍ dū̱tam i̍va̱ vāca̍m iṣya upa̱stire̱ śvaita̍rīṁ dhe̱num ī̍ḻe | ye vāta̍jūtās ta̱raṇi̍bhi̱r evai̱ḥ pari̱ dyāṁ sa̱dyo a̱paso̍ babhū̱vuḥ ||
english: I send forth speech toward the Ṛbhus like a messenger; I praise the white cow as their undergirding. Goaded by the wind with swift energies, they instantly encompassed heaven with their works.

sanskrit: ya̱dāra̱m akra̍nn ṛ̱bhava̍ḥ pi̱tṛbhyā̱m pari̍viṣṭī ve̱ṣaṇā̍ da̱ṁsanā̍bhiḥ | ād id de̱vānā̱m upa̍ sa̱khyam ā̍ya̱n dhīrā̍saḥ pu̱ṣṭim a̍vahan ma̱nāyai̍ ||
english: When the Ṛbhus worked the wonder for their parents — adorning and encompassing them with marvels — then indeed they came to the friendship of the gods; the wise ones carried prosperity to Manā.

sanskrit: puna̱r ye ca̱kruḥ pi̱tarā̱ yuvā̍nā̱ sanā̱ yūpe̍va jara̱ṇā śayā̍nā | te vājo̱ vibhvā̍m̐ ṛ̱bhur indra̍vanto̱ madhu̍psaraso no 'vantu ya̱jñam ||
english: They who made their aged parents young again, who lay as old as the sacrificial post — may Vāja, Vibhvan, Ṛbhu, attended by Indra, dripping with sweetness, protect our sacrifice.

sanskrit: yat sa̱ṁvatsa̍m ṛ̱bhavo̱ gām ara̍kṣa̱n yat sa̱ṁvatsa̍m ṛ̱bhavo̱ mā api̍ṁśan | yat sa̱ṁvatsa̱m abha̍ra̱n bhāso̍ asyā̱s tābhi̱ḥ śamī̍bhir amṛta̱tvam ā̍śuḥ ||
english: For a year the Ṛbhus guarded the cow; for a year the Ṛbhus fashioned it; for a year they gathered her splendors — through those labors they attained immortality.

sanskrit: jye̱ṣṭha ā̍ha cama̱sā dvā ka̱reti̱ kanī̍yā̱n trīn kṛ̍ṇavā̱mety ā̍ha | ka̱ni̱ṣṭha ā̍ha ca̱tura̍s ka̱reti̱ tvaṣṭa̍ ṛbhava̱s tat pa̍naya̱d vaco̍ vaḥ ||
english: The eldest said, 'Let us make the one cup into two'; the middle one said, 'Let us make three'; the youngest said, 'Let us make four' — Tvaṣṭṛ, O Ṛbhus, wondered at that speech of yours.

sanskrit: sa̱tyam ū̍cu̱r nara̍ e̱vā hi ca̱krur anu̍ sva̱dhām ṛ̱bhavo̍ jagmur e̱tām | vi̱bhrāja̍mānām̐ś cama̱sām̐ ahe̱vāve̍na̱t tvaṣṭā̍ ca̱turo̍ dadṛ̱śvān ||
english: Rightly they spoke, and so indeed they did; the Ṛbhus followed their own nature along that path. Tvaṣṭṛ, seeing the four gleaming cups, wondered as if at a marvel.

sanskrit: dvāda̍śa̱ dyūn yad ago̍hyasyāti̱thye raṇa̍nn ṛ̱bhava̍ḥ sa̱santa̍ḥ | su̱kṣetrā̍kṛṇva̱nn ana̍yanta̱ sindhū̱n dhanvāti̍ṣṭha̱nn oṣa̍dhīr ni̱mnam āpa̍ḥ ||
english: For twelve days the Ṛbhus lay sleeping as the guests of Agohya; they made good fields, led rivers along, caused deserts to bloom with plants, sent waters downward.

sanskrit: ratha̱ṁ ye ca̱kruḥ su̱vṛta̍ṁ nare̱ṣṭhāṁ ye dhe̱nuṁ vi̍śva̱juva̍ṁ vi̱śvarū̍pām | ta ā ta̍kṣantv ṛ̱bhavo̍ ra̱yiṁ na̱ḥ svava̍sa̱ḥ svapa̍saḥ su̱hastā̍ḥ ||
english: Those who fashioned the chariot that runs smoothly to win the prize for men, who fashioned the cow of all forms that gives all nourishment — may the Ṛbhus fashion riches for us, self-helping, skillful-working, with dexterous hands.

sanskrit: apo̱ hy e̍ṣā̱m aju̍ṣanta de̱vā a̱bhi kratvā̱ mana̍sā̱ dīdhyā̍nāḥ | vājo̍ de̱vānā̍m abhavat su̱karmendra̍sya ṛbhu̱kṣā varu̍ṇasya̱ vibhvā̍ ||
english: The gods, reflecting on their skill with mind and purpose, came to take pleasure in their works. Vāja became the favored one of the gods for good deeds, Ṛbhukṣan of Indra, and Vibhvan of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: ye harī̍ me̱dhayo̱kthā mada̍nta̱ indrā̍ya ca̱kruḥ su̱yujā̱ ye aśvā̍ | te rā̱yas poṣa̱ṁ dravi̍ṇāny a̱sme dha̱tta ṛ̍bhavaḥ kṣema̱yanto̱ na mi̱tram ||
english: Those who, praised in hymns with sacrificial meat, gladden Indra — who fashioned for him the well-yoked bay steeds — may those Ṛbhus bestow on us increase of riches and wealth, even as a friend in peaceful time.

sanskrit: i̱dāhna̍ḥ pī̱tim u̱ta vo̱ mada̍ṁ dhu̱r na ṛ̱te śrā̱ntasya̍ sa̱khyāya̍ de̱vāḥ | te nū̱nam a̱sme ṛ̍bhavo̱ vasū̍ni tṛ̱tīye̍ a̱smin sava̍ne dadhāta ||
english: The gods said there could be no drinking or rejoicing without the labor of the weary and the friendship of the divine; now, therefore, O Ṛbhus, lay down your treasures for us at this third pressing.

sanskrit: ṛ̱bhur vibhvā̱ vāja̱ indro̍ no̱ acche̱maṁ ya̱jñaṁ ra̍tna̱dheyopa̍ yāta | i̱dā hi vo̍ dhi̱ṣaṇā̍ de̱vy ahnā̍m adhā̍t pī̱tiṁ sam madā̍ agmatā vaḥ ||
english: Ṛbhu, Vibhvan, Vāja — and Indra — come to us, come to this sacrifice for the bestowing of treasures. For the divine Dhiṣaṇā has apportioned the drinking of days for you; come together to the exhilarations.

sanskrit: vi̱dā̱nāso̱ janma̍no vājaratnā u̱ta ṛ̱tubhi̍r ṛbhavo mādayadhvam | saṁ vo̱ madā̱ agma̍ta̱ sam pura̍ṁdhiḥ su̱vīrā̍m a̱sme ra̱yim era̍yadhvam ||
english: O Ṛbhus, prize-winners by birth, be exhilarated also with the libations offered at the right seasons; may your exhilarations converge, may your abundance converge — send to us riches with fine heroes.

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ vo̍ ya̱jña ṛ̍bhavo 'kāri̱ yam ā ma̍nu̱ṣvat pra̱divo̍ dadhi̱dhve | pra vo 'cchā̍ jujuṣā̱ṇāso̍ asthu̱r abhū̍ta̱ viśve̍ agri̱yota vā̍jāḥ ||
english: This sacrifice has been prepared for you, O Ṛbhus, which from of old you have undertaken here, as among humans; those who have delighted in you come forward to you — all of you were the foremost, and the prize-winners.

sanskrit: abhū̍d u vo vidha̱te ra̍tna̱dheya̍m i̱dā na̍ro dā̱śuṣe̱ martyā̍ya | piba̍ta vājā ṛbhavo da̱de vo̱ mahi̍ tṛ̱tīya̱ṁ sava̍na̱m madā̍ya ||
english: There has come the bestowing of treasures for your worshipper, O heroes, for the mortal who offers gifts. Drink, O Vājas, O Ṛbhus — the great third pressing has been given to you for exhilaration.

sanskrit: ā vā̍jā yā̱topa̍ na ṛbhukṣā ma̱ho na̍ro̱ dravi̍ṇaso gṛṇā̱nāḥ | ā va̍ḥ pī̱tayo̍ 'bhipi̱tve ahnā̍m i̱mā asta̍ṁ nava̱sva̍ iva gman ||
english: Come to us, O Vājas; come here, O Ṛbhukṣan, O great heroes praised for your wealth. Your drinkings come at the proper times of the days, even as these have come home like newcomers.

sanskrit: ā na̍pātaḥ śavaso yāta̱nope̱maṁ ya̱jñaṁ nama̍sā hū̱yamā̍nāḥ | sa̱joṣa̍saḥ sūrayo̱ yasya̍ ca̱ stha madhva̍ḥ pāta ratna̱dhā indra̍vantaḥ ||
english: Come to us, O grandsons of Strength, invoked with reverence; drink the honey with the inspired sages whose company you keep, O jewel-givers who have Indra with you.

sanskrit: sa̱joṣā̍ indra̱ varu̍ṇena̱ soma̍ṁ sa̱joṣā̍ḥ pāhi girvaṇo ma̱rudbhi̍ḥ | a̱gre̱pābhi̍r ṛtu̱pābhi̍ḥ sa̱joṣā̱ gnāspatnī̍bhī ratna̱dhābhi̍ḥ sa̱joṣā̍ḥ ||
english: O Indra, drink the soma together with Varuṇa; O lover of songs, drink together with the Maruts — together with those who drink first, those who drink at the right seasons, together with the divine wives who bestow treasures.

sanskrit: sa̱joṣa̍sa ādi̱tyair mā̍dayadhvaṁ sa̱joṣa̍sa ṛbhava̱ḥ parva̍tebhiḥ | sa̱joṣa̍so̱ daivye̍nā savi̱trā sa̱joṣa̍sa̱ḥ sindhu̍bhī ratna̱dhebhi̍ḥ ||
english: Be exhilarated together with the Ādityas, O Ṛbhus; be exhilarated together with the mountains; together with divine Savitṛ; together with the rivers that bestow treasures.

sanskrit: ye a̱śvinā̱ ye pi̱tarā̱ ya ū̱tī dhe̱nuṁ ta̍ta̱kṣur ṛ̱bhavo̱ ye aśvā̍ | ye aṁsa̍trā̱ ya ṛdha̱g roda̍sī̱ ye vibhvo̱ nara̍ḥ svapa̱tyāni̍ ca̱kruḥ ||
english: Those who as Aśvins, those who as fathers, those who as helpers — the Ṛbhus who fashioned the cow and the horses, who joined the two hemispheres, who on Vibhvan's side, the heroes, wrought excellent works for offspring.

sanskrit: ye goma̍nta̱ṁ vāja̍vantaṁ su̱vīra̍ṁ ra̱yiṁ dha̱ttha vasu̍mantam puru̱kṣum | te a̍gre̱pā ṛ̍bhavo mandasā̱nā a̱sme dha̍tta̱ ye ca̍ rā̱tiṁ gṛ̱ṇanti̍ ||
english: You who bestow riches rich in cattle, rich in prizes, rich in heroes, possessing treasures, and abundant — O Ṛbhus, foremost drinkers, exhilarated, bestow them on us and on those who praise generosity.

sanskrit: nāpā̍bhūta̱ na vo̍ 'tītṛṣā̱māni̍ḥśastā ṛbhavo ya̱jñe a̱smin | sam indre̍ṇa̱ mada̍tha̱ sam ma̱rudbhi̱ḥ saṁ rāja̍bhī ratna̱dheyā̍ya devāḥ ||
english: O Ṛbhus, you have not been diminished nor left without laud at this sacrifice; be exhilarated together with Indra, together with the Maruts, together with kings, O gods, for the bestowing of treasures.

sanskrit: i̱hopa̍ yāta śavaso napāta̱ḥ saudha̍nvanā ṛbhavo̱ māpa̍ bhūta | a̱smin hi va̱ḥ sava̍ne ratna̱dheya̱ṁ gama̱ntv indra̱m anu̍ vo̱ madā̍saḥ ||
english: Come here, O grandsons of Strength, O Saudhanvanā Ṛbhus; be not absent. For in this pressing the bestowing of jewels is yours; may your exhilarations follow Indra.

sanskrit: āga̍nn ṛbhū̱ṇām i̱ha ra̍tna̱dheya̱m abhū̱t soma̍sya̱ suṣu̍tasya pī̱tiḥ | su̱kṛ̱tyayā̱ yat sva̍pa̱syayā̍ ca̱m̐ eka̍ṁ vica̱kra ca̍ma̱saṁ ca̍tu̱rdhā ||
english: The bestowing of jewels has come here for the Ṛbhus, there has been the drinking of the well-pressed soma, because with skill and with beautiful craft one among them divided the one cup into four.

sanskrit: vy a̍kṛṇota cama̱saṁ ca̍tu̱rdhā sakhe̱ vi śi̱kṣety a̍bravīta | athai̍ta vājā a̱mṛta̍sya̱ panthā̍ṁ ga̱ṇaṁ de̱vānā̍m ṛbhavaḥ suhastāḥ ||
english: He divided the cup into four and said, 'Divide, O Friend, and share.' Then, O Vājas, O Ṛbhus of dexterous hands, you entered the path of immortality and the company of the gods.

sanskrit: ki̱mmaya̍ḥ svic cama̱sa e̱ṣa ā̍sa̱ yaṁ kāvye̍na ca̱turo̍ vica̱kra | athā̍ sunudhva̱ṁ sava̍na̱m madā̍ya pā̱ta ṛ̍bhavo̱ madhu̍naḥ so̱myasya̍ ||
english: Of what material was that cup which you divided into four by your wisdom? Now press out the pressing for exhilaration; drink of the sweet soma, O Ṛbhus.

sanskrit: śacyā̍karta pi̱tarā̱ yuvā̍nā̱ śacyā̍karta cama̱saṁ de̍va̱pāna̍m | śacyā̱ harī̱ dhanu̍tarāv ataṣṭendra̱vāhā̍v ṛbhavo vājaratnāḥ ||
english: By your power you made your parents young again; by your power you fashioned the cup for the gods to drink; by your power you carved the two swift bay steeds for Indra to drive — O Ṛbhus, O prize-winners.

sanskrit: yo va̍ḥ su̱noty a̍bhipi̱tve ahnā̍ṁ tī̱vraṁ vā̍jāsa̱ḥ sava̍na̱m madā̍ya | tasmai̍ ra̱yim ṛ̍bhava̱ḥ sarva̍vīra̱m ā ta̍kṣata vṛṣaṇo mandasā̱nāḥ ||
english: He who presses for you the strong pressing at the proper time of day for exhilaration — for him, O Ṛbhus, O bulls, exhilarated, fashion riches with all heroes.

sanskrit: prā̱taḥ su̱tam a̍pibo haryaśva̱ mādhya̍ṁdina̱ṁ sava̍na̱ṁ keva̍laṁ te | sam ṛ̱bhubhi̍ḥ pibasva ratna̱dhebhi̱ḥ sakhī̱m̐r yām̐ i̍ndra cakṛ̱ṣe su̍kṛ̱tyā ||
english: You drank the morning pressing, O Indra of bay steeds; the midday pressing was exclusively yours; drink now together with the Ṛbhus who bestow treasures — those friends whom you made by your skillful deeds, O Indra.

sanskrit: ye de̱vāso̱ abha̍vatā sukṛ̱tyā śye̱nā i̱ved adhi̍ di̱vi ni̍ṣe̱da | te ratna̍ṁ dhāta śavaso napāta̱ḥ saudha̍nvanā̱ abha̍vatā̱mṛtā̍saḥ ||
english: You who, through your skillful deeds, became as gods and sat in heaven like eagles — bestow jewels, O grandsons of Strength, O Saudhanvanas who have become immortal.

sanskrit: yat tṛ̱tīya̱ṁ sava̍naṁ ratna̱dheya̱m akṛ̍ṇudhvaṁ svapa̱syā su̍hastāḥ | tad ṛ̍bhava̱ḥ pari̍ṣiktaṁ va e̱tat sam made̍bhir indri̱yebhi̍ḥ pibadhvam ||
english: That third pressing with its jewel-bestowing which you, dexterous-handed, fashioned with beautiful craft — O Ṛbhus, that is poured out for you; drink together of the exhilarating, strength-giving draughts.

sanskrit: a̱na̱śvo jā̱to a̍nabhī̱śur u̱kthyo̱3̱̍ ratha̍s trica̱kraḥ pari̍ vartate̱ raja̍ḥ | ma̱hat tad vo̍ de̱vya̍sya pra̱vāca̍na̱ṁ dyām ṛ̍bhavaḥ pṛthi̱vīṁ yac ca̱ puṣya̍tha ||
english: Born without horses, without reins, worthy of invocation — the three-wheeled chariot rolls through the firmament. Great is that proclamation of your divine nature, O Ṛbhus, when you nourish both heaven and earth.

sanskrit: ratha̱ṁ ye ca̱kruḥ su̱vṛta̍ṁ su̱ceta̱so 'vi̍hvaranta̱m mana̍sa̱s pari̱ dhyayā̍ | tām̐ ū̱ nv a1̱̍sya sava̍nasya pī̱taya̱ ā vo̍ vājā ṛbhavo vedayāmasi ||
english: Those who with clear minds and intent meditation fashioned the chariot that runs smoothly without swerving — O Vājas, O Ṛbhus, we now make known to you the drinkings of this pressing.

sanskrit: tad vo̍ vājā ṛbhavaḥ supravāca̱naṁ de̱veṣu̍ vibhvo abhavan mahitva̱nam | jivrī̱ yat santā̍ pi̱tarā̍ sanā̱jurā̱ puna̱r yuvā̍nā ca̱rathā̍ya̱ takṣa̍tha ||
english: O Vājas, O Ṛbhus, that which is well-proclaimed for you has become great among the gods through Vibhvan — when, as both aged parents were worn out with old age, you fashioned them young again to walk about.

sanskrit: eka̱ṁ vi ca̍kra cama̱saṁ catu̍rvaya̱ṁ niś carma̍ṇo̱ gām a̍riṇīta dhī̱tibhi̍ḥ | athā̍ de̱veṣv a̍mṛta̱tvam ā̍naśa śru̱ṣṭī vā̍jā ṛbhava̱s tad va̍ u̱kthya̍m ||
english: One made the single cup into four; they released the cow from the skin by their understanding. Thus they attained immortality among the gods — O obedient Vājas, O Ṛbhus, that is your worthy deed.

sanskrit: ṛ̱bhu̱to ra̱yiḥ pra̍tha̱maśra̍vastamo̱ vāja̍śrutāso̱ yam ajī̍jana̱n nara̍ḥ | vi̱bhva̱ta̱ṣṭo vi̱dathe̍ṣu pra̱vācyo̱ yaṁ de̍vā̱so 'va̍thā̱ sa vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
english: The riches fashioned by the Ṛbhus, first in fame, renowned for prizes — which the heroes generated; fashioned by Vibhvan, to be proclaimed at assemblies — whom the gods protect, he is all-seeing.

sanskrit: sa vā̱jy arvā̱ sa ṛṣi̍r vaca̱syayā̱ sa śūro̱ astā̱ pṛta̍nāsu du̱ṣṭara̍ḥ ||
english: He is the prize-winning steed, he is the seer through eloquence, he is the hero and archer irresistible in battles — he whom Vāja, Vibhvan, and the Ṛbhus have favored.

sanskrit: śreṣṭha̍ṁ va̱ḥ peśo̱ adhi̍ dhāyi darśa̱taṁ stomo̍ vājā ṛbhava̱s taṁ ju̍juṣṭana | dhīrā̍so̱ hi ṣṭhā ka̱vayo̍ vipa̱ścita̱s tān va̍ e̱nā brahma̱ṇā ve̍dayāmasi ||
english: The most beautiful and visible form has been placed on you; O Vājas, O Ṛbhus, be pleased with that hymn of praise. For you are the wise, the poets, the discerning — with this sacred utterance we make it known to you.

sanskrit: yū̱yam a̱smabhya̍ṁ dhi̱ṣaṇā̍bhya̱s pari̍ vi̱dvāṁso̱ viśvā̱ naryā̍ṇi̱ bhoja̍nā | dyu̱manta̱ṁ vāja̱ṁ vṛṣa̍śuṣmam utta̱mam ā no̍ ra̱yim ṛ̍bhavas takṣa̱tā vaya̍ḥ ||
english: You who know all the enjoyments that are fit for men, with your intelligence — fashion for us, O Ṛbhus, the radiant, vigorous, supreme battle-prize; shape riches and vigorous life for us.

sanskrit: i̱ha pra̱jām i̱ha ra̱yiṁ rarā̍ṇā i̱ha śravo̍ vī̱rava̍t takṣatā naḥ | yena̍ va̱yaṁ ci̱taye̱māty a̱nyān taṁ vāja̍ṁ ci̱tram ṛ̍bhavo dadā naḥ ||
english: Bestowing here offspring, here riches, fashion here for us heroic glory; that splendid prize by which we may distinguish ourselves above others — give that to us, O Ṛbhus.

sanskrit: upa̍ no vājā adhva̱ram ṛ̍bhukṣā̱ devā̍ yā̱ta pa̱thibhi̍r deva̱yānai̍ḥ | yathā̍ ya̱jñam manu̍ṣo vi̱kṣv ā̱3̱̍su da̍dhi̱dhve ra̍ṇvāḥ su̱dine̍ṣv ahnā̍m ||
english: Come, O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣan, O gods, to our sacrifice along the god-traveled paths — as you have joyfully established the sacrifice of Manu among his peoples on the good days of the days.

sanskrit: te vo̍ hṛ̱de mana̍se santu ya̱jñā juṣṭā̍so a̱dya ghṛ̱tani̍rṇijo guḥ ||
english: May these sacrifices today be pleasing to your heart and mind, lustrous with ghee; may the poured-out ones, the well-beloved, go to you.

sanskrit: tryu̱dā̱yaṁ de̱vahi̍ta̱ṁ yathā̍ va̱ḥ stomo̍ vājā ṛbhukṣaṇo da̱de va̍ḥ | ju̱hve ma̍nu̱ṣvad upa̍rāsu vi̱kṣu yu̱ṣme sacā̍ bṛ̱haddi̍veṣu̱ soma̍m ||
english: As the hymn of praise placed by the gods has been given to you three times daily, O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣan, so I pour the soma in the highest worlds, among the peoples, after the manner of Manu, with you present, on the great days.

sanskrit: pīvo̍aśvāḥ śu̱cadra̍thā̱ hi bhū̱tāya̍ḥśiprā vājinaḥ suni̱ṣkāḥ | indra̍sya sūno śavaso napā̱to 'nu̍ vaś cety agri̱yam madā̍ya ||
english: For you have been the well-fed steeds with radiant chariots, wearing lovely necklaces, prize-winners. O sons of Indra, O grandsons of Strength, the foremost exhilaration comes after you.

sanskrit: ṛ̱bhum ṛ̍bhukṣaṇo ra̱yiṁ vāje̍ vā̱jinta̍ma̱ṁ yuja̍m | indra̍svantaṁ havāmahe sadā̱sāta̍mam a̱śvina̍m ||
english: We invoke Ṛbhu, Ṛbhukṣan, the richest prize-winning companion in the race — him who ever wins the gain, who has Indra with him, the horse-possessor.

sanskrit: sed ṛ̍bhavo̱ yam ava̍tha yū̱yam indra̍ś ca̱ martya̍m | sa dhī̱bhir a̍stu̱ sani̍tā me̱dhasā̍tā̱ so arva̍tā ||
english: That mortal whom you and Indra protect, O Ṛbhus — may he be a winner through his wisdom, a winner of sacrificial food, a winner through his steed.

sanskrit: vi no̍ vājā ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ pa̱thaś ci̍tana̱ yaṣṭa̍ve | a̱smabhya̍ṁ sūrayaḥ stu̱tā viśvā̱ āśā̍s tarī̱ṣaṇi̍ ||
english: O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣan, discern paths for us to sacrifice; O inspired ones who are praised, let us cross all the quarters.

sanskrit: taṁ no̍ vājā ṛbhukṣaṇa̱ indra̱ nāsa̍tyā ra̱yim | sam aśva̍ṁ carṣa̱ṇibhya̱ ā pu̱ru śa̍sta ma̱ghatta̍ye ||
english: O Vājas, O Ṛbhukṣan, O Indra, O Nāsatyas — bring together for us that wealth, bring together the horse for the peoples, greatly acclaimed for the winning of bounty.

sanskrit: u̱to hi vā̍ṁ dā̱trā santi̱ pūrvā̱ yā pū̱rubhya̍s tra̱sada̍syur nito̱śe | kṣe̱trā̱sāṁ da̍dathur urvarā̱sāṁ gha̱naṁ dasyu̍bhyo a̱bhibhū̍tim u̱gram ||
english: Indeed, the gifts that are the earlier ones exist for you two — those which Trasadasyu received from the Pūrus' line; you gave to him the fields, the fertile lands, and the fierce overwhelming weapon against the Dasyus.

sanskrit: u̱ta vā̱jina̍m puruni̱ṣṣidhvā̍naṁ dadhi̱krām u̍ dadathur vi̱śvakṛ̍ṣṭim | ṛ̱ji̱pyaṁ śye̱nam pru̍ṣi̱tapsu̍m ā̱śuṁ ca̱rkṛtya̍m a̱ryo nṛ̱pati̱ṁ na śūra̍m ||
english: You also gave Dadhikrā, the prize-winning steed widely restrained, the conqueror of all tribes — the straight-coursing, falcon-like, dappled, swift, ever-active, noble, lord-of-men-like hero.

sanskrit: yaṁ sī̱m anu̍ pra̱vate̍va̱ drava̍nta̱ṁ viśva̍ḥ pū̱rur mada̍ti̱ harṣa̍māṇaḥ | pa̱ḍbhir gṛdhya̍ntam medha̱yuṁ na śūra̍ṁ ratha̱tura̱ṁ vāta̍m iva̱ dhraja̍ntam ||
english: Him whom, as he runs swiftly as down a slope, every man delights in exultantly — as he strives with his hooves like a hero eager for the sacrifice, swift in the chariot, rushing like the wind.

sanskrit: yaḥ smā̍rundhā̱no gadhyā̍ sa̱matsu̱ sanu̍tara̱ś cara̍ti̱ goṣu̱ gaccha̍n | ā̱virṛ̍jīko vi̱dathā̍ ni̱cikya̍t ti̱ro a̍ra̱tim pary āpa̍ ā̱yoḥ ||
english: He who, bridled, moves in battles running ever forward going among the cattle — Ṛjīka manifest, discerning at assemblies, has encompassed the one who resists Āyu from all sides.

sanskrit: u̱ta smai̍naṁ vastra̱mathi̱ṁ na tā̱yum anu̍ krośanti kṣi̱tayo̱ bhare̍ṣu | nī̱cāya̍māna̱ṁ jasu̍ri̱ṁ na śye̱naṁ śrava̱ś cācchā̍ paśu̱mac ca̍ yū̱tham ||
english: The peoples also cry after him in battles as after a cloth-picker-thief — as he swoops down like an exhausted falcon toward glory and a herd of cattle.

sanskrit: u̱ta smā̍su pratha̱maḥ sa̍ri̱ṣyan ni ve̍veti̱ śreṇi̍bhī̱ rathā̍nām | sraja̍ṁ kṛṇvā̱no janyo̱ na śubhvā̍ re̱ṇuṁ reri̍hat ki̱raṇa̍ṁ dada̱śvān ||
english: And him, as he runs first in the ranks of chariots, do they ever acclaim — making a garland, adorning himself like a festive man, repeatedly scattering dust, spreading rays of light.

sanskrit: u̱ta sya vā̱jī sahu̍rir ṛ̱tāvā̱ śuśrū̍ṣamāṇas ta̱nvā̍ sama̱rye | tura̍ṁ ya̱tīṣu̍ tu̱raya̍nn ṛji̱pyo 'dhi̍ bhru̱voḥ ki̍rate re̱ṇum ṛ̱ñjan ||
english: And that prize-winner, mighty, faithful to the rite, listening with his body in the contest — the straight-going one making swift the swift ones among the striving, scatters dust from his brows as he rushes.

sanskrit: u̱ta smā̍sya tanya̱tor i̍va̱ dyor ṛ̍ghāya̱to a̍bhi̱yujo̍ bhayante | ya̱dā sa̱hasra̍m a̱bhi ṣī̱m ayo̍dhīd du̱rvartu̍ḥ smā bhavati bhī̱ma ṛ̱ñjan ||
english: And as when the thunder of the sky roars, those who attack him fear him — when he fights a thousand, he becomes the fearsome, difficult-to-restrain one, rushing headlong.

sanskrit: u̱ta smā̍sya panayanti̱ janā̍ jū̱tiṁ kṛ̍ṣṭi̱pro a̱bhibhū̍tim ā̱śoḥ | u̱taina̍m āhuḥ sami̱the vi̱yanta̱ḥ parā̍ dadhi̱krā a̍sarat sa̱hasrai̍ḥ ||
english: And people admire the swift impulse of the swift one who overwhelms the tribes; and they say of him as they are spent in battle, 'Dadhikrā has galloped past with thousands.'

sanskrit: ā da̍dhi̱krāḥ śava̍sā̱ pañca̍ kṛ̱ṣṭīḥ sūrya̍ iva̱ jyoti̍ṣā̱pas ta̍tāna | sa̱ha̱sra̱sāḥ śa̍ta̱sā vā̱jy arvā̍ pṛ̱ṇaktu̱ madhvā̱ sam i̱mā vacā̍ṁsi ||
english: Dadhikrā with his strength has encompassed the five peoples like the sun with its light upon the waters. May that prize-winning steed, winner of thousands, winner of hundreds, fill these speeches with sweetness.

sanskrit: ā̱śuṁ da̍dhi̱krāṁ tam u̱ nu ṣṭa̍vāma di̱vas pṛ̍thi̱vyā u̱ta ca̍rkirāma | u̱cchantī̱r mām u̱ṣasa̍ḥ sūdaya̱ntv ati̱ viśvā̍ni duri̱tāni̍ parṣan ||
english: That swift Dadhikrā let us now praise and let us make him go round in heaven and on earth. May the dawns as they rise be good to me; may they lead me past all troubles.

sanskrit: ma̱haś ca̍rka̱rmy arva̍taḥ kratu̱prā da̍dhi̱krāvṇa̍ḥ puru̱vāra̍sya̱ vṛṣṇa̍ḥ | yam pū̱rubhyo̍ dīdi̱vāṁsa̱ṁ nāgniṁ da̱dathu̍r mitrāvaruṇā̱ tatu̍rim ||
english: I celebrate greatly the course of the steed Dadhikrāvan, full of purpose, with many boons, a bull — him who, shining like fire for the Pūrus, Mitra and Varuṇa gave to the swift.

sanskrit: yo aśva̍sya dadhi̱krāvṇo̱ akā̍rī̱t sami̍ddhe a̱gnā u̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭau | anā̍gasa̱ṁ tam adi̍tiḥ kṛṇotu̱ sa mi̱treṇa̱ varu̍ṇenā sa̱joṣā̍ḥ ||
english: He who has offered praise of the horse Dadhikrāvan at the kindled fire at the shining of the dawn — may Aditi make him sinless; may he be in harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: da̱dhi̱krāvṇa̍ i̱ṣa ū̱rjo ma̱ho yad ama̍nmahi ma̱rutā̱ṁ nāma̍ bha̱dram | sva̱staye̱ varu̍ṇam mi̱tram a̱gniṁ havā̍maha̱ indra̱ṁ vajra̍bāhum ||
english: In remembering the great food and refreshment of Dadhikrāvan and the auspicious name of the Maruts, we invoke Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, and Indra of the thunderbolt-arm for well-being.

sanskrit: indra̍m i̱ved u̱bhaye̱ vi hva̍yanta u̱dīrā̍ṇā ya̱jñam u̍papra̱yanta̍ḥ | da̱dhi̱krām u̱ sūda̍na̱m martyā̍ya da̱dathu̍r mitrāvaruṇā no̱ aśva̍m ||
english: Both sides called upon Indra — urging on the sacrifice, roused to action; and Mitra and Varuṇa gave Dadhikrā, the sweetener, to us as a horse for mortal man.

sanskrit: da̱dhi̱krāvṇo̍ akāriṣaṁ ji̱ṣṇor aśva̍sya vā̱jina̍ḥ | su̱ra̱bhi no̱ mukhā̍ kara̱t pra ṇa̱ āyū̍ṁṣi tāriṣat ||
english: I have praised Dadhikrāvan, the conquering, prize-winning horse. May he make our mouths fragrant; may he prolong our life-spans.

sanskrit: da̱dhi̱krāvṇa̱ id u̱ nu ca̍rkirāma̱ viśvā̱ in mām u̱ṣasa̍ḥ sūdayantu | a̱pām a̱gner u̱ṣasa̱ḥ sūrya̍sya̱ bṛha̱spate̍r āṅgira̱sasya̍ ji̱ṣṇoḥ ||
english: Now indeed let us make Dadhikrāvan go round; may all the dawns be favorable to me — the dawns of the Waters, of Agni, of the Sun, of Bṛhaspati the Āṅgirasa, of the conqueror.

sanskrit: satvā̍ bhari̱ṣo ga̍vi̱ṣo du̍vanya̱sac chra̍va̱syād i̱ṣa u̱ṣasa̍s turaṇya̱sat | sa̱tyo dra̱vo dra̍va̱raḥ pa̍taṁga̱ro da̍dhi̱krāveṣa̱m ūrja̱ṁ sva̍r janat ||
english: A true warrior, bearing forward, seeking cattle, ever-serviceable, hastening after glory and refreshment, dwelling with the dawns — the true, swift, ever-moving, bird-like Dadhikrāvan has generated food, energy, and light.

sanskrit: u̱ta smā̍sya̱ drava̍tas turaṇya̱taḥ pa̱rṇaṁ na ver anu̍ vāti praga̱rdhina̍ḥ | śye̱nasye̍va̱ dhraja̍to aṅka̱sam pari̍ dadhi̱krāvṇa̍ḥ sa̱horjā tari̍trataḥ ||
english: And as he runs swiftly, eagerly, a feather blows after him like a bird's — around Dadhikrāvan rushing like a falcon, going across with his strength and energy.

sanskrit: u̱ta sya vā̱jī kṣi̍pa̱ṇiṁ tu̍raṇyati grī̱vāyā̍m ba̱ddho a̍pika̱kṣa ā̱sani̍ | kratu̍ṁ dadhi̱krā anu̍ sa̱ṁtavī̍tvat pa̱thām aṅkā̱ṁsy anv ā̱panī̍phaṇat ||
english: And that prize-winner hastens with his swift-cutting line tied to his neck and flanks; Dadhikrā, stretching out his purpose, paws the turnings of the paths.

sanskrit: ha̱ṁsaḥ śu̍ci̱ṣad vasu̍r antarikṣa̱sad dhotā̍ vedi̱ṣad ati̍thir duroṇa̱sat | nṛ̱ṣad va̍ra̱sad ṛ̍ta̱sad vyo̍ma̱sad a̱bjā go̱jā ṛ̍ta̱jā a̍dri̱jā ṛ̱tam ||
english: The swan settled in the pure, the Vasu settled in the atmosphere, the Hotṛ settled on the altar, the guest settled in the dwelling — the one settled among men, settled in the best, settled in the rite, settled in the sky — born of the water, born of the cow, born of the rite, born of the mountain — it is ṛta, the cosmic order.

sanskrit: indrā̱ ko vā̍ṁ varuṇā su̱mnam ā̍pa̱ stomo̍ ha̱viṣmā̍m̐ a̱mṛto̱ na hotā̍ | yo vā̍ṁ hṛ̱di kratu̍mām̐ a̱smad u̱ktaḥ pa̱sparśa̍d indrāvaruṇā̱ nama̍svān ||
english: O Indra and Varuṇa, who attains your favor? The hymn of praise offering oblations, the immortal like a Hotṛ — he who, reverent, has touched our speech which is full of purpose in your hearts, O Indrāvaruṇā.

sanskrit: indrā̍ ha̱ yo varu̍ṇā ca̱kra ā̱pī de̱vau marta̍ḥ sa̱khyāya̱ praya̍svān | sa ha̍nti vṛ̱trā sa̍mi̱theṣu̱ śatrū̱n avo̍bhir vā ma̱hadbhi̱ḥ sa pra śṛ̍ṇve ||
english: O Indra and Varuṇa, the mortal who has made you both his close companions, O gods, bringing offerings for friendship — he slays foes in battles and enemies with great aids, and he becomes widely famous.

sanskrit: indrā̍ ha̱ ratna̱ṁ varu̍ṇā̱ dheṣṭhe̱tthā nṛbhya̍ḥ śaśamā̱nebhya̱s tā | yadī̱ sakhā̍yā sa̱khyāya̱ somai̍ḥ su̱tebhi̍ḥ supra̱yasā̍ mā̱dayai̍te ||
english: O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bestow the richest treasures thus on men who have exerted themselves, when the two friends exhilarate themselves joyfully with pressed soma-draughts for the sake of friendship.

sanskrit: indrā̍ yu̱vaṁ va̍ruṇā di̱dyum a̍smi̱nn oji̍ṣṭham ugrā̱ ni va̍dhiṣṭa̱ṁ vajra̍m | yo no̍ du̱revo̍ vṛ̱kati̍r da̱bhīti̱s tasmi̍n mimāthām a̱bhibhū̱ty oja̍ḥ ||
english: O Indra and Varuṇa, the two of you, mighty ones, strike down with the most powerful thunderbolt here in this one the mischievous; on him who is ill-willing toward us, a deceiver and betrayer — pour out overwhelming strength.

sanskrit: indrā̍ yu̱vaṁ va̍ruṇā bhū̱tam a̱syā dhi̱yaḥ pre̱tārā̍ vṛṣa̱bheva̍ dhe̱noḥ | sā no̍ duhīya̱d yava̍seva ga̱tvī sa̱hasra̍dhārā̱ paya̍sā ma̱hī gauḥ ||
english: O Indra and Varuṇa, be the impellers forward of this thought, like two bulls of a milk-cow; may she, having gone like a barley-field, that great cow with a thousand streams, milk milk for us.

sanskrit: to̱ke hi̱te tana̍ya u̱rvarā̍su̱ sūro̱ dṛśī̍ke̱ vṛṣa̍ṇaś ca̱ pauṁsye̍ | indrā̍ no̱ atra̱ varu̍ṇā syātā̱m avo̍bhir da̱smā pari̍takmyāyām ||
english: When children are placed on fertile fields, when the sun is sighted, when the bulls show their manly strength — may Indra and Varuṇa be with us here with their aids, the wondrous ones in this encompassing struggle.

sanskrit: yu̱vām id dhy ava̍se pū̱rvyāya̱ pari̱ prabhū̍tī ga̱viṣa̍ḥ svāpī | vṛ̱ṇī̱mahe̍ sa̱khyāya̍ pri̱yāya̱ śūrā̱ maṁhi̍ṣṭhā pi̱tare̍va śa̱mbhū ||
english: For ancient aid we choose you two, who are very powerful, and the self-help of the one seeking cattle; O most bountiful heroes, beneficent like fathers, we choose you for dear friendship.

sanskrit: tā vā̱ṁ dhiyo 'va̍se vāja̱yantī̍r ā̱jiṁ na ja̍gmur yuva̱yūḥ su̍dānū | śri̱ye na gāva̱ upa̱ soma̍m asthu̱r indra̱ṁ giro̱ varu̍ṇam me manī̱ṣāḥ ||
english: These thoughts seeking your aid, striving for the prize, have gone to you two like a race — longing for you, O bounteous givers; like cows to adorn, they have stood by the soma; my hymns approach Indra and Varuṇa.

sanskrit: i̱mā indra̱ṁ varu̍ṇam me manī̱ṣā agma̱nn upa̱ dravi̍ṇam i̱cchamā̍nāḥ | upe̍m asthur jo̱ṣṭāra̍ iva̱ vasvo̍ ra̱ghvīr i̍va̱ śrava̍so̱ bhikṣa̍māṇāḥ ||
english: These thoughts of mine have come to Indra and Varuṇa, seeking riches; they have stood near, like those who rejoice in wealth, like light ones begging for glory.

sanskrit: aśvya̍sya̱ tmanā̱ rathya̍sya pu̱ṣṭer nitya̍sya rā̱yaḥ pata̍yaḥ syāma | tā ca̍krā̱ṇā ū̱tibhi̱r navya̍sībhir asma̱trā rāyo̍ ni̱yuta̍ḥ sacantām ||
english: May we be lords of the flourishing that belongs to horses and to chariots, of the wealth that is one's own. May those two, performing with ever-fresh aids, let their teams of wealth come hither to us.

sanskrit: ā no̍ bṛhantā bṛha̱tībhi̍r ū̱tī indra̍ yā̱taṁ va̍ruṇa̱ vāja̍sātau | yad di̱dyava̱ḥ pṛta̍nāsu pra̱krīḻā̱n tasya̍ vāṁ syāma sani̱tāra̍ ā̱jeḥ ||
english: O Indra, O Varuṇa, come to us, the two mighty ones with mighty aids, in the winning of the prize; when the bright ones play forward in battles, may we be the winners of that race of yours.

sanskrit: mama̍ dvi̱tā rā̱ṣṭraṁ kṣa̱triya̍sya vi̱śvāyo̱r viśve̍ a̱mṛtā̱ yathā̍ naḥ | kratu̍ṁ sacante̱ varu̍ṇasya de̱vā rājā̍mi kṛ̱ṣṭer u̍pa̱masya̍ va̱vreḥ ||
english: Mine is the royal kingdom of the ruling warrior class — of both worlds — all the immortals are with us; the gods follow the purpose of Varuṇa. I am the king of the uppermost layer of earth.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ rājā̱ varu̍ṇo̱ mahya̱ṁ tāny a̍su̱ryā̍ṇi pratha̱mā dhā̍rayanta | kratu̍ṁ sacante̱ varu̍ṇasya de̱vā rājā̍mi kṛ̱ṣṭer u̍pa̱masya̍ va̱vreḥ ||
english: I am King Varuṇa; those first powers of lordship were conferred on me; the gods follow the will of Varuṇa. I am the king of the uppermost layer of earth.

sanskrit: a̱ham indro̱ varu̍ṇa̱s te ma̍hi̱tvorvī ga̍bhī̱re raja̍sī su̱meke̍ | tvaṣṭe̍va̱ viśvā̱ bhuva̍nāni vi̱dvān sam ai̍raya̱ṁ roda̍sī dhā̱raya̍ṁ ca ||
english: I am Indra, O Varuṇa — through your greatness the two wide deep atmospheres are well-established; like Tvaṣṭṛ knowing all worlds, I set in motion and sustain the two world-halves.

sanskrit: a̱ham a̱po a̍pinvam u̱kṣamā̍ṇā dhā̱raya̱ṁ diva̱ṁ sada̍na ṛ̱tasya̍ | ṛ̱tena̍ pu̱tro adi̍ter ṛ̱tāvo̱ta tri̱dhātu̍ prathaya̱d vi bhūma̍ ||
english: I swelled the waters as they were watering; I hold the sky, the seat of the cosmic order. By the ṛta, the son of Aditi, faithful to ṛta, spread the earth wide in its threefold nature.

sanskrit: māṁ nara̱ḥ svaśvā̍ vā̱jaya̍nto̱ māṁ vṛ̱tāḥ sa̱mara̍ṇe havante | kṛ̱ṇomy ā̱jim ma̱ghavā̱ham indra̱ iya̍rmi re̱ṇum a̱bhibhū̍tyojāḥ ||
english: Men with fine horses, striving for the prize, call upon me; those who are chosen call upon me in the encounter. I, the bountiful Indra, make the race; I raise the dust with overwhelming strength.

sanskrit: a̱haṁ tā viśvā̍ cakara̱ṁ naki̍r mā̱ daivya̱ṁ saho̍ varate̱ apra̍tītam | yan mā̱ somā̍so ma̱mada̱n yad u̱kthobhe bha̍yete̱ raja̍sī apā̱re ||
english: I did all those things; none resists my divine, irresistible power — when the somas exhilarated me and both the infinite atmospheres feared my utterances.

sanskrit: vi̱duṣ ṭe̱ viśvā̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ tasya̱ tā pra bra̍vīṣi̱ varu̍ṇāya vedhaḥ | tvaṁ vṛ̱trāṇi̍ śṛṇviṣe jagha̱nvān tvaṁ vṛ̱tām̐ a̍riṇā indra̱ sindhū̍n ||
english: Knowing all the worlds of him, O wise one, declare those words to Varuṇa; you are heard, O Indra, as the slayer of obstructions; you have set the rivers free, cleaving through what blocked them.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̱m atra̍ pi̱tara̱s ta ā̍san sa̱pta ṛṣa̍yo daurga̱he ba̱dhyamā̍ne | ta āya̍janta tra̱sada̍syum asyā̱ indra̱ṁ na vṛ̍tra̱tura̍m ardhade̱vam ||
english: Our fathers were then the seven seers who were bound in the stronghold of the oppressor; they sacrificed for Trasadasyu of this lineage — Indra-like in slaying enemies, a half-divine being.

sanskrit: pu̱ru̱kutsā̍nī̱ hi vā̱m adā̍śad dha̱vyebhi̍r indrāvaruṇā̱ namo̍bhiḥ | athā̱ rājā̍naṁ tra̱sada̍syum asyā vṛtra̱haṇa̍ṁ dadathur ardhade̱vam ||
english: For Purukutsānī gave to you both with oblations and reverences, O Indrāvaruṇā; and so you gave to this lineage King Trasadasyu, the Vṛtra-slayer, the half-divine being.

sanskrit: rā̱yā va̱yaṁ sa̍sa̱vāṁso̍ madema ha̱vyena̍ de̱vā yava̍sena̱ gāva̍ḥ | tāṁ dhe̱num i̍ndrāvaruṇā yu̱vaṁ no̍ vi̱śvāhā̍ dhatta̱m ana̍pasphurantīm ||
english: Exhilarated with riches may we rejoice, O gods, with our oblations; the cattle with their food. That cow, O Indrāvaruṇā — the one who does not kick — set her for us for all days.

sanskrit: ka u̍ śravat kata̱mo ya̱jñiyā̍nāṁ va̱ndāru̍ de̱vaḥ ka̍ta̱mo ju̍ṣāte | kasye̱māṁ de̱vīm a̱mṛte̍ṣu̱ preṣṭhā̍ṁ hṛ̱di śre̍ṣāma suṣṭu̱tiṁ su̍ha̱vyām ||
english: Who among the divine ones will hear? Which of the worthy of worship is the most pleased to receive praise? To whom shall we fasten in our heart this most beloved of the immortals, this beautiful hymn with fine oblations?

sanskrit: ko mṛ̍ḻāti kata̱ma āga̍miṣṭho de̱vānā̍m u kata̱maḥ śambha̍viṣṭhaḥ | ratha̱ṁ kam ā̍hur dra̱vada̍śvam ā̱śuṁ yaṁ sūrya̍sya duhi̱tāvṛ̍ṇīta ||
english: Who shows favor? Which one of the gods is easiest to reach? Which one is most beneficent? Of which one's chariot, with swift horses, do they speak — which one did the daughter of the Sun choose?

sanskrit: ma̱kṣū hi ṣmā̱ gaccha̍tha̱ īva̍to̱ dyūn indro̱ na śa̱ktim pari̍takmyāyām | di̱va ājā̍tā di̱vyā su̍pa̱rṇā kayā̱ śacī̍nām bhavatha̱ḥ śaci̍ṣṭhā ||
english: For you travel swiftly through many days, like Indra's power in the contest that goes about; born from heaven, you heavenly birds of beautiful wings — by what power of all your powers are you most powerful?

sanskrit: kā vā̍m bhū̱d upa̍māti̱ḥ kayā̍ na̱ āśvi̍nā gamatho hū̱yamā̍nā | ko vā̍m ma̱haś ci̱t tyaja̍so a̱bhīka̍ uru̱ṣyata̍m mādhvī dasrā na ū̱tī ||
english: What offering has there been for you? By what shall you come to us when invoked, O Aśvins? Who has confronted even your great abandonment? O sweet ones, O wondrous ones, protect us with your aid.

sanskrit: u̱ru vā̱ṁ ratha̱ḥ pari̍ nakṣati̱ dyām ā yat sa̍mu̱drād a̱bhi varta̍te vām | madhvā̍ mādhvī̱ madhu̍ vām pruṣāya̱n yat sī̍ṁ vā̱m pṛkṣo̍ bhu̱raja̍nta pa̱kvāḥ ||
english: Your wide chariot goes round the sky, as it turns toward you from the ocean; O sweet ones, sweet honey is sprinkled for you, when ripened fruits have nourished you with their fullness.

sanskrit: sindhu̍r ha vāṁ ra̱sayā̍ siñca̱d aśvā̍n ghṛ̱ṇā vayo̍ 'ru̱ṣāsa̱ḥ pari̍ gman | tad ū̱ ṣu vā̍m aji̱raṁ ce̍ti̱ yāna̱ṁ yena̱ patī̱ bhava̍thaḥ sū̱ryāyā̍ḥ ||
english: The Sindhu poured the Rasā upon your horses; red birds, gleaming with heat, went about; that swift-moving vehicle of yours is well-known, by which you became the husbands of Sūryā.

sanskrit: i̱heha̱ yad vā̍ṁ sama̱nā pa̍pṛ̱kṣe seyam a̱sme su̍ma̱tir vā̍jaratnā | u̱ru̱ṣyata̍ṁ jari̱tāra̍ṁ yu̱vaṁ ha̍ śri̱taḥ kāmo̍ nāsatyā yuva̱drik ||
english: When those of equal birth have met here and there and this good will with its prize-treasure is ours — protect the praiser; for the desire of the one who has sought refuge leans toward you, O Nāsatyas.

sanskrit: taṁ vā̱ṁ ratha̍ṁ va̱yam a̱dyā hu̍vema pṛthu̱jraya̍m aśvinā̱ saṁga̍ti̱ṁ goḥ | yaḥ sū̱ryāṁ vaha̍ti vandhurā̱yur girvā̍hasam puru̱tama̍ṁ vasū̱yum ||
english: That chariot of yours we would summon today, O Aśvins — the wide-ranging chariot that encounters the cow, which carries Sūryā in the living wicker-work, the hymn-bearing, most-praised one, seeking wealth.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ śriya̍m aśvinā de̱vatā̱ tāṁ divo̍ napātā vanatha̱ḥ śacī̍bhiḥ | yu̱vor vapu̍r a̱bhi pṛkṣa̍ḥ sacante̱ vaha̍nti̱ yat ka̍ku̱hāso̱ rathe̍ vām ||
english: You two, O Aśvins, O divine sons of heaven, win that divine splendor through your powers; the abundances accompany your beauty, when the proud ones carry you in your chariot.

sanskrit: ko vā̍m a̱dyā ka̍rate rā̱taha̍vya ū̱taye̍ vā suta̱peyā̍ya vā̱rkaiḥ ||
english: Who today has made an offering of sacrificial call for your aid, or for the drinking of the pressed soma with songs of praise, or for the winning of the cosmic order's ancient favor, becoming reverent toward the Aśvins?

sanskrit: hi̱ra̱ṇyaye̍na purubhū̱ rathe̍ne̱maṁ ya̱jñaṁ nā̍sa̱tyopa̍ yātam | pibā̍tha̱ in madhu̍naḥ so̱myasya̱ dadha̍tho̱ ratna̍ṁ vidha̱te janā̍ya ||
english: O Nāsatyas, who exist manifoldly, come to this sacrifice in your golden chariot; drink of the sweetness of the soma and bestow the jewel on the worshipping people.

sanskrit: ā no̍ yātaṁ di̱vo acchā̍ pṛthi̱vyā hi̍ra̱ṇyaye̍na su̱vṛtā̱ rathe̍na | mā vā̍m a̱nye ni ya̍man deva̱yanta̱ḥ saṁ yad da̱de nābhi̍ḥ pū̱rvyā vā̍m ||
english: Come to us from the sky, from the earth, in your golden, well-rolling chariot; let not others who worship the gods hold you back, when the ancient hub of your chariot joins.

sanskrit: nū no̍ ra̱yim pu̍ru̱vīra̍m bṛ̱hanta̱ṁ dasrā̱ mimā̍thām u̱bhaye̍ṣv a̱sme | naro̱ yad vā̍m aśvinā̱ stoma̱m āva̍n sa̱dhastu̍tim ājamī̱ḻhāso̍ agman ||
english: Now fashion for us, O wondrous ones, great riches with many heroes in both spheres; when men have sent forth the hymn to you both, O Aśvins, those who press the soma together have come with joint praise.

sanskrit: i̱heha̱ yad vā̍ṁ sama̱nā pa̍pṛ̱kṣe seyam a̱sme su̍ma̱tir vā̍jaratnā | u̱ru̱ṣyata̍ṁ jari̱tāra̍ṁ yu̱vaṁ ha̍ śri̱taḥ kāmo̍ nāsatyā yuva̱drik ||
english: When those of equal birth have met here and there, and this good will with its prize-treasure is ours — protect the praiser; for the desire of the one who has sought refuge leans toward you, O Nāsatyas.
